title: Kidney - Anatomy Lecture
department_desc: Anatomy and embryonic development of the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra
matrix_title: TWISTED MEDICINE LECTURE 1 - HIGH-YIELD ANATOMICAL PEARLS & BOARD EXAM MATRIX

summary_table.content: • Vertebral Extent: T12 to L3; Right Kidney is -1.5 cm lower due to right hepatic lobe. • Dimensions: 12 × 6 × 3 cm. Average weight: 150 g in males, 135 g in females. • Hilum: Vertical slit at medial border opposite L1 (Transpyloric plane).

• Hilum Order (Ant to Post): Vein -> Artery - Pelvis (V-A-P). • 4 Protective Layers: (1) Fibrous capsule (strips easily in health), (2) Perirenal fat, (3) Gerota's renal fascia (splits into anterior Toldt & posterior Zuckerkandl), (4) Pararenal fat. • Critical Point: Gerota's fascia remains open INFERIORLY -> allows extravasated pus/urine/blood to track into pelvis.

• Ribs: Left Kidney related to 11th & 12th ribs; Right Kidney related ONLY to 12th rib. • 3 Muscles (Medial to Lateral): Psoas major -> Quadratus lumborum -> Transversus abdominis. • 3 Nerves: Subcostal (T12), Iliohypogastric (L1), Ilioinguinal (L1).
• Right Kidney: Suprarenal, Liver (peritoneal), 2nd part Duodenum (non-peritoneal), Right Colic Flexure (non-peritoneal), Small
• Left Kidney: Suprarenal, Stomach (peritoneal, lesser sac), Spleen, Pancreatic tail (non-peritoneal), Left Colic Flexure & Descending Colon (non-peritoneal), Jejunum (peritoneal).

• 5 Segmental End-Arteries: Apical, Upper, Middle, Lower, Posterior (NO anastomoses -> infarction upon occlusion). • Brodel's Line: Longitudinal avascular line along posterior lateral border -> ideal for nephrolithotomy. • Nutcracker Syndrome: Compression of Left Renal Vein between SMA and Aorta -> left flank pain, hematuria, and left testicular
